content.text:
## Recommendation

Pick up [#128: prevent stored DOM injection in match rendering](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/128) next, split into two ordered slices.

The first slice should be:

`fix(frontend): render persisted matches safely`

- Replace the match-card `innerHTML` construction with DOM APIs and `textContent`. The current sink directly interpolates persisted IDs, names, locations, breeds, URLs, and scores into markup: [match-dashboard.js](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/petspotr/cmd/web-frontend/static/js/match-dashboard.js:41).
- Validate and restrict image sources before assigning `src`.
- Coerce and bound IDs, dates, statuses, and numeric score values.
- Add browser coverage with hostile HTML, quote, URL, and script-like field values, asserting they remain inert.
- Complete the required UI review, verifier, and code-review gates.
- Open the PR as `Part of #128`.

A second slice should externalize inline handlers/styles and add the restrictive CSP and baseline response headers needed to close #128. Keeping that separate prevents a security fix from turning into a repository-wide styling rewrite.

Why this is next:

- `main` is clean and exactly synchronized with protected remote `main` at `7a7d990`; there are currently no open PRs.
- The finding remains present in current code, while the API returns stored match records directly: [server.go](/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/petspotr/cmd/web-frontend/server.go:597).
- It has no architectural or external-service dependency.
- It becomes directly exposed once [#115](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/115) starts persisting real, user-derived match data, so fixing it first avoids building new product behavior on an unsafe renderer.

After #128, I would follow this product sequence:

1. [#114](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/114) — canonical, versioned report schemas.
2. [#113](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/113) — route browser reports through the canonical services.
3. [#115](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/115) — match real candidates and persist real matches.
4. [#110](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/110) — identity and ownership, after selecting an identity provider and splitting the large issue into reviewable slices.

I would not prioritize the small CI/docs chores such as [#150](https://github.com/scottdensmore/PetSpotR/issues/150) or #146 ahead of product and security work.

The issue tracker also needs reconciliation: #123 appears delivered by PR #143; #104/#105 refer to repository-inspection tests removed by PR #151; #106/#127 reference planning documents removed by PR #149; and #107/#66 are substantially implemented. Those should be closed or narrowed, but not via a separate development PR.

One operational note: the configured `gh` credential is invalid. Public read-only triage worked, but authentication must be refreshed before issue updates, pushing, or opening a PR.

No files were changed and no test suites were run during this triage.
